justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 and circulation requirements through Catalogue Management Component, File Storage Container (for digital assets via AWS S3 EU-Central), Circulation Engine Component, and patron-facing Circulation & Self-Service Component in the SPA.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The <800ms SLA (R-05) is addressed via Search Container (Elasticsearch 8.x), Hot Data Cache Component (Redis), Debezium CDC streaming, State Management & Caching Store (TanStack Query), and Connection Pooler (PgBouncer).
justifications.compatibility: The Integration Service container provides dedicated adapters (SIS Sync Component, IoT Gateway Component, Payment Adapter Component) supporting open standards (MQTT, SFTP, REST, AMQP) to interface seamlessly with University SIS, RFID Gates, and Stripe EU.
justifications.usability: The Web Application (SPA) comprehensively serves patrons and staff via Catalogue & Search UI, Circulation & Self-Service Component, and Notification & Feedback Component, although mobile channels referenced at Level 1 are omitted in lower levels.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance and recovery are thoroughly designed using Resilience4j Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component, Dead Letter & Retry Component in Message Broker, PostgreSQL Read Replica, and automated RDS Backup & Snapshot Manager.
justifications.security: EU data residency and security are enforced via Geo-Routing & Compliance Filter, Data Purge & Compliance Worker (GDPR), Virus & Malware Scanner Service, TLS 1.3, and pgaudit in Audit & Security Monitor.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular separation exists across dedicated containers and components. Schema evolution is isolated via Database Schema Migration Engine, while asynchronous event decoupling via Message Broker and Debezium CDC maintains low architectural coupling.
justifications.portability: Standard technologies (Spring Boot, Envoy, React, Celery, PostgreSQL) offer strong portability, though some components are coupled to specific AWS services like AWS S3 EU-Central and AWS ElastiCache for Redis.

PERF-01.justification: Elasticsearch deployed across three availability zones alongside Redis hot data caching and gRPC gateway routing directly satisfy sub-800ms search latency under peak load.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios and Elasticsearch query optimization under peak load.
tradeoffs: Aggressive caching improves query response times but introduces potential data staleness.

PERF-02.justification: Debezium CDC asynchronously captures transactional database updates and streams them to Elasticsearch workers, decoupling cataloguing writes from searches and ensuring fast index refresh.
sensitivity_points: Debezium CDC streaming lag and Elasticsearch near-real-time index refresh rates.
tradeoffs: Asynchronous indexing prevents search latency degradation at the expense of temporary eventual consistency.

AVAIL-01.justification: The Search Engine Core is a multi-AZ cluster with circuit breaking and fallback caching. Furthermore, loan transactions run against PostgreSQL, completely isolated from search node failures.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch index replica factor and fast failover between cluster nodes.
tradeoffs: Multi-AZ clustering increases infrastructure footprint and inter-AZ data transfer costs.

AVAIL-02.justification: The frontend SPA and Envoy API Gateway route traffic around failed backend instances. Centralized Redis session storage and ACID PostgreSQL transactions prevent interruption or lost loans.
sensitivity_points: Envoy health check responsiveness and automatic instance eviction speed.
tradeoffs: Externalizing state to Redis enables fast failover but creates a shared service dependency.

MOD-01.justification: The Integration Service provides modular adapter patterns for external providers. However, catalogue ingestion flows and metadata transformations might require slight coordination with Core Services.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling provider-specific digital schemas within the integration adapter layer.
tradeoffs: Isolating external logic into dedicated adapters adds network hop latency to ingest.

MOD-02.justification: The Circulation Engine is implemented as a standard Spring Bean without any dynamic rules engine, external policy store, or configuration mechanism to modify rules at runtime without redeployment.
sensitivity_points: Absence of runtime rule configuration or policy engine abstractions.
tradeoffs: Compiling circulation rules into code maximizes execution speed but hampers operational modifiability.

SEC-01.justification: EU data residency is enforced by design across all components via the perimeter Geo-Routing filter, EU-locked AWS RDS/S3 infrastructure, and EU-specific external integrations.
sensitivity_points: Strict regional locking in cloud IAM and boundary routing filters.
tradeoffs: Mandating EU-only residency prevents utilizing multi-region disaster recovery outside the EU.

SEC-02.justification: Access is blocked by Spring Security authorization checks at the core service level, while unauthorized attempts are captured and recorded by the Audit Component and pgaudit monitor.
sensitivity_points: Fine-grained patron record ownership validation in Spring Security.
tradeoffs: Comprehensive database and security audit logging increases storage utilization and write overhead.
